the pride of San Diego, Ron's town
Thin steak marinated in lime, garlic and cumin, grilled and chopped over crisp fries with melted cheese, guacamole and sour cream.
Brick's French onion dip and chips

Onions cooked low and slow until jammy, folded through sour cream and cream cheese with chives and a dash of Worcestershire, with thick-cut salted chips. Cook 3 thinly sliced brown onions in 40g butter over low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and jammy. Cool completely. Beat 250g sour cream with 125g cream cheese, 1 tsp Worcestershire, garlic powder and salt, then fold in the onions and chopped chives. Chill 1 hour so the flavour comes through. Serve with 2 large bags of thick-cut salted chips.
M: Stay classy, San Diego. Mild chicken tacos for the news team.
Crispy oven-baked chicken in warm corn tortillas with cabbage, fresh tomato salsa and lime crema. Mild enough for the whole news team.
Ron takes Veronica out on the town

Sirloin seared and butter basted with garlic and thyme, with a loaded baked potato, creamy garlic spinach and a peppercorn sauce. Bake 4 potatoes at 200C for 1 hour. Season 4 sirloins and sear in a smoking pan 3 minutes a side, add 40g butter, garlic and thyme and baste until 54C inside, then rest. Add 1 tbsp cracked pepper and 150ml cream to the pan and simmer 2 minutes. Wilt 400g spinach with garlic, add 100ml cream and 30g parmesan and reduce. Split the potatoes and top with sour cream and chives.
W: Warm self-saucing butterscotch pudding with golden syrup, dark brown sugar and vanilla ice cream.
K: Ron's newsroom exclamation, with a blackberry twist.
Homemade blackberry and lemon syrup topped with sparkling water over ice. A deep burgundy drink for the whole family.

dishes.make_ahead: Make on the day, serve warm

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C conventional and grease a deep 1.5L baking dish with a little of the butter.
Whisk the flour with part of the sugar and the salt, then whisk melted butter, milk, egg and vanilla in another bowl and fold together just until combined.
Spread into the dish. Mix the rest of the sugar with the cornflour and sprinkle over the batter.
Dissolve the golden syrup in the boiling water and pour gently over the back of a spoon without stirring.
Bake on a tray until the sponge is set and a skewer in the sponge comes out clean. The sauce stays underneath.
Rest, then scoop into bowls with the warm butterscotch sauce and vanilla ice cream. All the butterscotch flavour, no whisky.

ingredients.item: lemons, juiced to give 60ml, plus slices to serve

s.note: the dog ate a whole wheel, Ron isn't even mad
s.how: Score the top of a 500g brie wheel. Drizzle with 2 tbsp honey, scatter thyme and 50g walnuts and bake at 180C for 15 minutes until molten. Serve with crackers. Baxter would approve.

s.note: the pride of San Diego, Ron's town
s.how: Marinate 500g skirt steak in juice of 2 limes, 2 garlic cloves and 1 tsp cumin for 1 hour, grill hot 3 minutes a side and chop. Bake 750g frozen fries until crisp, cover with 150g grated Monterey Jack and grill to melt. Top with the steak, 1 mashed avocado and 100g sour cream.

m.note: Stay classy, San Diego. Mild chicken tacos for the news team.
m.how: For four, cut 600g chicken breast into strips. Coat in 60g plain flour mixed with 1 tsp smoked paprika and 0.5 tsp ground cumin, dip in 2 beaten eggs, then press into 100g panko breadcrumbs. Arrange on a lined tray, drizzle with 2 tbsp olive oil and bake at 220C for 18-22 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and the thickest piece reaches 75C. Mix 150g sour cream with the juice of 1 lime. Dice 2 tomatoes and 0.5 onion and toss with the juice of a second lime. Warm 12 corn tortillas according to the packet. Fill with chicken, 200g shredded cabbage, tomato salsa and lime crema. Keep any chilli on the side.

w.how: Serves four. Heat the oven to 180C conventional (160C fan-forced). Grease a deep 1.5L baking dish with 10g butter. Whisk 150g self-raising flour with 75g dark brown sugar and a pinch of salt. In another bowl whisk 50g melted butter, 125ml milk, 1 egg and 1 tsp vanilla extract. Fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients just until combined and spread into the dish. Mix 100g dark brown sugar with 1 tbsp cornflour and sprinkle evenly over the batter. Dissolve 2 tbsp golden syrup in 250ml boiling water. Gently pour over the back of a spoon onto the pudding without stirring. Place the dish on a baking tray and bake for 30-35 minutes, until the sponge is set and a skewer inserted into the sponge comes out clean; sauce will remain underneath. Rest for 5 minutes, then scoop into four bowls with the warm butterscotch sauce and a scoop of vanilla ice cream each. All the butterscotch flavour, no whisky.

d.note: Ron's newsroom exclamation, with a blackberry twist.
d.how: For four, gently simmer 125g blackberries with 40g caster sugar and 60ml water for 5 minutes, crushing the berries. Strain and cool completely. Divide the syrup and 60ml lemon juice between four ice-filled glasses. Top with 800ml chilled sparkling water and stir. Taste and add a little more sugar if needed. Serve with lemon slices. No alcohol.
